summary: Privacy-focused Tauri browser shell with passing automated validation and a canonical human-verified packaged macOS WebView validation covering HTTPS-only navigation, blocked HTTP navigation and downloads, sandboxing, policy badges, and decision logging. This cycle fixed several silent-failure and correctness bugs (unhandled Tauri command errors, an isolation-scope cleanup leak, a disconnected vault bookmark count), corrected UI/audit-log claims that overstated session isolation as real per-profile cookie/storage separation — it is currently TypeScript-layer bookkeeping only, since the app runs a single shared WebView — replaced the encrypted-export passphrase key derivation with salted Argon2id (was an unsalted XOR-fold that left most key bytes at zero for short passphrases), moved the permission and download decision registries from in-memory-only to SQLite persistence, and added SQLCipher at-rest encryption for the live database with the key stored in the OS keychain (existing unencrypted databases get a clean-slate reset, not an in-place migration -- see docs/recommendations/SQLCIPHER_KEYCHAIN_SCOPE.md for why).
current_objective: Keep the validated packaged WebView privacy boundary honest: fix concrete bugs and false claims as found, without adding new browser subsystems or capability scope.
known_gaps: Session isolation (per-profile cookies/localStorage/IndexedDB) is not implemented at the WebView/storage level — there is one shared Tauri window/WebView, so all profiles currently share the same browser storage. Tracked honestly in src/app/threatModel.ts under doesNotProtectAgainst.

WebView permission/download callback integration is not implemented -- the live WebView is a plain iframe with no camera/mic/download grants for policy to callback-integrate with. Blocked on the same native-webview architecture gap as session isolation.
constraints: Do not add a new browser subsystem during validation.
Do not weaken download blocking or permission prompting.
Do not treat smoke tests as proof of packaged desktop behavior.
Manual validation must use bounded, non-sensitive test URLs and content.
Do not let UI copy, audit events, or the threat model claim privacy guarantees (e.g. storage isolation) that aren't actually implemented.
